messages:
maria-ruiz: quick check — running into intermittent auth handshake failures when the Node SDK talks to a private endpoint behind our proxy. It only fails on streaming connections that last >30s, non-stream requests are fine. anyone seen this?
kevin-cho: hmm, do you have logs? 401 or TLS error?
maria-ruiz: logs show repeated `401 Unauthorized` during the stream, followed by `stream reset`. snippet: `2026-03-15T10:12:34Z ERROR grpc: stream error: code: Unauthenticated desc: token expired or invalid`
annie-lam: is the token being refreshed mid-stream? long-lived streams keep the same headers; if the proxy terminates and re-establishes, the reconnected request won't have a fresh token unless client reauths.
maria-ruiz: token refresh happens on the SDK side, but the stream isn't triggering refresh callback — it relies on the initial bearer header. SDK is v0.9.7 Node.
samir-khan: we had similar with our Go client when proxy did connection pooling + keepalive and reused an idle upstream connection after auth TTL on the server. Workaround was to set `Connection: keep-alive` + send short periodic no-op pings so proxy doesn't swap backend.
annie-lam: also check proxy idle timeout and any token-introspection TTL on the private endpoint. If the edge enforces short session lifetime and proxy replays the CONNECT without auth, you'll see 401 on reconnect.
kevin-cho: can you paste the client config? specifically PROXY_HOST, private base URL, and whether you're using mTLS or just bearer. redact tokens.
maria-ruiz: config: `PRIVATE_BASE_URL=https://internal.redwood.local`, `PROXY=http://10.23.45.6:3128`, mTLS=false, SDK env `REDWOOD_SDK_MODE=private`. Using fetch-stream wrapper from the SDK.
kevin-cho: try enabling `SDK_RECONNECT_BACKOFF=2000` and `STREAM_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL=15s` (env flags are experimental in 0.9.7). That forced periodic headers refresh for us.
annie-lam: alternative: switch to direct VPC peering or set proxy to forward the `Authorization` on re-connection (some proxies drop auth when reusing backend sockets). Our infra team added `preserve-auth: true` in the proxy for a while.
maria-ruiz: good pointers. quick test: I switched proxy to preserve-auth and ran a 2-minute stream — no 401s so far.
samir-khan: cool. FYI for language quirk: Node's http/1.1 agent will reuse sockets aggressively; you can set `agent: new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 1 })` to limit reuse. Go's default client behaves different.
kevin-cho: filing a small follow-up PR to SDK to surface a `streamKeepaliveInterval` option and document proxy recommendations. pinging @infra to confirm if `preserve-auth` is safe for customer setups. :thumbsup:
dev-bot: infra ticket #INF-421 created and linked to thread.
maria-ruiz: thanks all — will leave this running and report back if anything else pops up.
